sentences.text: The specific name honors the long pennaceous feathers located on the animal's metatarsus.
The longest feathers on its foot measured about 55 mm, which is slightly shorter than the length of the metatarsus itself.
A second toe bore an enlarged claw that was shortened and less developed than the sickle-shaped claws found in related species.
Evidence suggests shorter feathers covered the long foot plumes, indicating the presence of coverts similar to those seen in modern birds.
The genus was first described by Xu and Zhang in the year 2005.
Fossils were unearthed from the Daohugou Bed within the Tiaojishan Formation in the regions of Hebei and Liaoning, China.
The specific epithet daohugouensis identifies the Daohugou locality where the holotype specimen was discovered.
Pedopenna was probably a carnivore that hunted insects, small reptiles, and mammals.
Xu and Zhang suggested in 2005 that the foot feathers could be ornamental or vestigial.
Recent studies have recovered Pedopenna as a scansoriopterygid.
This animal is classified under the class Reptilia.
It belongs to Paraves, a group of maniraptoran dinosaurs that includes birds and their closest relatives.

Pedopenna lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 163 million years ago in the Callovian stage, in what is now Asia, though recent radiometric dating places it at approximately 168 million years ago, with an estimated time range between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
However, recent radiometric dating places Pedopenna in the middle Jurassic Callovian, approximately 168 million years ago.
The estimated time range for this taxon spans between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
Pedopenna is possibly older than Archaeopteryx, although the exact age of the Daohugou Beds where it was found is debated.
It is debated whether Pedopenna is as old as Archaeopteryx, depending on the age of the Daohugou Bed.
Xu and Zhang postulated that Asia is the cradle of the origin of birds based on the presence of this basal avian lineage member.
